boards.title: Claimed by 9am: 10 Study Spots Worth Showing Up Early For
boards.description: Ten named study environments documented by Saint Joseph’s University, spanning focused, sensory-supportive, collaborative and technology-enabled settings.

cards.title: Quiet Study Area
cards.subtitle: Second Floor, Drexel Library
cards.notes: Settle into the designated quiet-study zone on Drexel’s second floor; use it for reading or solo work and keep conversations elsewhere.
cards.short_summary: A map-listed second-floor quiet-study area in Drexel Library.
cards.evidence_claim: The John R. Post Academic Center floor plan labels a Quiet Study area on the second floor of Drexel Library.
cards.source_title: John R. Post ’60 Academic Center Floor Plan
cards.access_notes: Located inside the Post Learning Commons and Drexel Library; visitor entry requires calling the service desk and showing photo ID.

cards.title: Sensory Room
cards.subtitle: First Floor, Drexel Library
cards.notes: Use this dedicated quiet room when focus or self-regulation would help; its listed tools include a sound machine and noise-blocking headphones.
cards.short_summary: A first-floor quiet room with sensory-support resources.
cards.evidence_claim: SJU Libraries identifies a first-floor Drexel Library Sensory Room for focus, self-regulation, decompression and meditation, with sensory resources.
cards.access_notes: Located in Drexel Library; library computers and SJU Wi-Fi are restricted to the Saint Joseph’s community.

cards.title: Sensory Friendly Seating
cards.subtitle: Second Floor, Drexel Library
cards.notes: Look for the egg chairs and low rockers on Drexel’s second floor when you want a quieter seated setup for individual study.
cards.short_summary: Second-floor egg chairs and low rockers intended for lounging or quiet study.
cards.evidence_claim: SJU Libraries directs users to egg chairs and low rockers on Drexel Library’s second floor for lounging or quiet study.
cards.access_notes: Located in Drexel Library; check current library access and building hours before going.

cards.title: Hawk Hill Study Rooms
cards.subtitle: Post Learning Commons & Drexel Library
cards.notes: Book a room through LibCal for a group of two or more; bring your work, then use the supplied whiteboard, markers and eraser.
cards.short_summary: Twenty-two reservable Hawk Hill rooms for group project work.
cards.evidence_claim: SJU Libraries lists 22 study rooms at Hawk Hill and states that study rooms are for groups of two or more and include whiteboards, markers and erasers.
cards.access_notes: Reserve through LibCal; reservations are limited to two hours and require confirmation from an SJU email. Unchecked-out rooms may be used until needed.

cards.title: Post Learning Commons Atrium
cards.subtitle: Post Learning Commons, Hawk Hill
cards.notes: Use one of the atrium’s three corner areas when an open shared setting fits your work; reserve it through the library’s student process.
cards.short_summary: An atrium with three corner areas available for student reservations.
cards.evidence_claim: SJU’s Library & Learning Commons page lists three corner areas in the Post Learning Commons Atrium under student reservations.
cards.access_notes: Student reservation space; request space through the library’s reservation process and check current building access before visiting.

cards.title: Post Learning Commons Lounges
cards.subtitle: Post Learning Commons, Hawk Hill
cards.notes: Choose a lounge when your project benefits from a larger shared setup; the university lists lounge capacities ranging from eight to 40.
cards.short_summary: Student-reservable lounges with capacities from eight to 40.
cards.evidence_claim: SJU’s Library & Learning Commons page lists Post Learning Commons Lounges for student reservations with capacities of eight to 40.
cards.access_notes: Student reservation space; use the library’s request-space process and confirm availability for your group.

cards.title: Post Learning Commons Terrace
cards.subtitle: Post Learning Commons, Hawk Hill
cards.notes: Plan a shared study session on the terrace when outdoor conditions suit your work; submit a student reservation request before relying on it.
cards.short_summary: A named Post Learning Commons terrace available for student reservations.
cards.evidence_claim: SJU’s Library & Learning Commons page lists the Post Learning Commons Terrace among student-reservable spaces.
cards.access_notes: Student reservation space; availability and weather may affect use, so request the space and verify access in advance.

cards.title: Griffith 208
cards.subtitle: Griffith Hall, University City
cards.notes: Use Griffith 208 for quiet individual work or course materials; the library describes it as a collection of rooms and areas outfitted for quiet study.
cards.short_summary: A University City library space outfitted as quiet study space.
cards.evidence_claim: SJU Libraries describes Griffith 208 as a large collection of rooms and areas fully outfitted as quiet study space for students.
cards.access_notes: Griffith Library is in Griffith Hall, Suite 208, at 600 S. 43rd St.; current students, faculty and staff have access to SJU computing and Wi‑Fi.

cards.title: Reading Room
cards.subtitle: Second Floor, Post Learning Commons
cards.notes: Bring longer reading or writing work to the two-story Reading Room, then spread out with materials at its tables or nearby work spaces.
cards.short_summary: A two-story second-floor reading room in the Post Learning Commons.
cards.evidence_claim: Saint Joseph’s Library Lines describes a two-story Reading Room on the second floor of the Post Learning Commons.
cards.source_title: Library Lines: Welcome to the Post Learning Commons
cards.access_notes: Inside the Post Learning Commons; visitor access is controlled and library building hours can change.

cards.title: Third-Floor Study Carrels
cards.subtitle: Third Floor, Post Learning Commons
cards.notes: Take a carrel on the third-floor balcony when you want a dedicated individual work surface; this level is described as the building’s quietest floor.
cards.short_summary: Individual study carrels lining the third-floor balcony.
cards.evidence_claim: Saint Joseph’s Library Lines states that the Post Learning Commons third-floor balcony is lined with spacious carrels and calls the third level the quietest floor.
cards.source_title: Library Lines: Welcome to the Post Learning Commons
cards.access_notes: Inside the Post Learning Commons; consult current library hours and controlled-entry rules before visiting.
